title: minReward==0 default silently opts out of the slippage guard
description: batchMint's minReward parameter (added by story-015 as a slippage guard against the M-01 MEV front-run) defaults to 0 for backward compatibility. A minReward of 0 disables the guard entirely (any payout, including zero, satisfies `nudgeAmount >= minReward`). An integrating front-end that omits/zeroes the parameter re-exposes M-01 in full: the honest minter is no longer protected and mints into an already-drained pot.
impact: Integration footgun. The slippage protection that story-015 introduced is opt-in by value: callers who do not set a non-zero minReward get no protection. A front-end or integrator that does not plumb the parameter through silently reverts the user to the unmitigated M-01 MEV exposure (mint cost + gas spent, no nudge received). No direct fund-at-risk in the contract itself; severity Low (integration / spec-deviation footgun).
attackPath: 1. Integrator calls batchMint without supplying minReward (or supplies 0), relying on the backward-compatible default.
2. The slippage guard is inert (nudgeAmount >= 0 always holds).
3. A searcher front-runs and captures the pot (M-01); the honest call succeeds and mints into an empty pot instead of reverting.
4. The user pays mint cost + gas and receives no nudge -- exactly the M-01 outcome story-015 intended to prevent.
recommendation: Make the slippage guard safe-by-default: either require an explicit minReward (no zero-default opt-out), or document prominently that minReward MUST be set to the caller's expected pot value and have integrating front-ends compute and pass it. Consider emitting an event or reverting when a qualifying batchMint is submitted with minReward==0 against a non-empty configured nudge pot.

metadata.note: NEW Low at run phoenix-nft-staking-14. No prior fingerprint. Distinct from M-01 (root cause = the opt-out default of the mitigation, not the MEV race itself).
